Perl (founded 1987) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Vikram Sarabhai is a physicist. Often regarded as the "Father of Indian space program", Sarabhai was honored with Padma Bhushan in 1966 and the Padma Vibhushan (posthumously) in 1972.
Which of these is a chemist?
Jan Baptist van Helmont is a chemist.
What is the atomic number of Nitrogen?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
In what year was Richard Feynman born?
Richard Feynman: Richard Phillips Feynman (May 11, 1918 – February 15, 1988) was an American theoretical physicist.
In what year was Special relativity discovered?
Special relativity: In physics, the special theory of relativity, or simply special relativity, is a scientific theory of the relationship between space and time.
In what year was Mustard gas discovered?
Mustard gas: There is no preventive agent against mustard gas, with protection depending entirely on skin and airways protection, and no antidote exists for mustard poisoning.
Sodium acetate: Pfizer. Sodium acetate is a chemical compound with formula CH3COONa, also abbreviated NaOAc.
Which country is Grumman F-14 Tomcat from?

Grumman F-14 Tomcat: United States. The Grumman F-14 Tomcat is an American carrier-capable supersonic, twin-engine, tandem two-seat, twin-tail, all-weather-capable variable-sweep wing fighter aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Radium?
Radium: Marie Curie. Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
Who is credited with discovering Saccharin?
Saccharin: Constantin Fahlberg. Saccharin, also called saccharine, benzosulfimide, or E954, or used in saccharin sodium or saccharin calcium forms, is a non-nutritive artificial sweetener.
Who is credited with discovering Chlorine?
Chlorine: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.

A central nervous system stimulant of the phenethylamine class, this combo medication is approved for narcolepsy and ADHD — but is also taken as an appetite suppressant and cognitive enhancer. What is it?
Adderall is the brand name of a fixed-dose combination medication used for the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy.
This cation forms when a proton attaches to ammonia, giving living organisms a vital source of nitrogen — what ion is it?
Ammonium is a modified form of ammonia that has an extra hydrogen atom.

Sitting at the milder end of a spectrum of diminished motivation — less severe than abulia and far short of akinetic mutism — this is a state marked by an absence of feeling, interest, or concern. What is it?
Apathy is a lack of feeling, emotion, interest, and/or concern about something.
These tiny prokaryotes fix nitrogen from the atmosphere, recycle nutrients, and handle the rotting of dead bodies — and they were among the very first life forms to appear on Earth. What are they?
Bacteria are ubiquitous, mostly free-living organisms often consisting of one biological cell.

A thin-leaved deciduous hardwood related to alders and hazels, this genus of trees is widespread across the Northern Hemisphere's temperate and boreal climates, typically as a short-lived pioneer species — name the tree?
Birch is a thin-leaved deciduous hardwood tree of the genus Betula, in the family Betulaceae, which also includes alders, hazels, and hornbeams.
Formed naturally through evaporation of saline water or generated by salt mining, which concentrated saltwater solution helps de-ice roads and preserve pickled foods?
Brine (or briny water) is a high-concentration solution of salt (typically sodium chloride or calcium chloride) in water.
Domesticated roughly 6,000 years ago in Mexico, this nightshade produces berries in red, green, and yellow ranging from mild to fiery — what is its scientific name?
Capsicum annuum is a flowering plant in the family Solanaceae (nightshades), native to the northern regions of South America and to southwestern North America.
Her famous experiment proved that parity is not conserved — yet the 1957 Nobel went to two male colleagues while she earned the first-ever Wolf Prize in Physics. Which Manhattan Project physicist?

Chien-Shiung Wu (pinyin: W Jinxing; May 31, 1912 - February 16, 1997) was a Chinese-American particle and experimental physicist who made significant contributions in the fields of nuclear and particle physics.
Native to Africa, Arabia and India, this semi-succulent herb smells like oregano and is known by names like Spanish thyme and Mexican mint — which plant?
Coleus amboinicus is a species of semi-succulent perennial plant in the family Lamiaceae.

The first anatomically modern humans known to inhabit Europe and Siberia, arriving as early as 56,800 years ago, this population interbred with the indigenous Neanderthals before the latter went extinct — who are they?
Cro-Magnon (EEMH) were the first early modern humans (Homo sapiens) found in Europe and Siberia, continuously occupying the continent possibly from as early as 56,800 years ago.
A colorless organosulfur compound known as the most widely used commercial sulfoxide, an important polar solvent. It leaves a distinctive taste when absorbed through the skin. What is it?
Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is an organosulfur compound with the formula (CH3)2S=O.

This is the industrial process of converting other forms of energy into electric power, typically at power plants using electromechanical devices, before it is transmitted and distributed to end users. What is this process called?
Electricity generation is the process of generating electric power from sources of primary energy.
This Hungarian-American physicist won the 1963 Nobel for applying fundamental symmetry principles to the atomic nucleus, having once worked as an assistant to David Hilbert at Göttingen. Who was he?
Eugene Wigner (November 17, 1902 - January 1, 1995) was a Hungarian-American theoretical physicist who also contributed to mathematical physics.
This omnivorous insect, common in North American homes, gets its name from ear-shaped hindwings and carries pincers on its abdomen — which species?
Forficula auricularia is a species complex comprising the common earwig.
The last living species in an order that first appeared over 290 million years ago, this disease-resistant "living fossil" with fan-shaped leaves is also called the maidenhair tree — which is it?
Ginkgo biloba (-goh), also known as the maidenhair tree, and often misspelled "gingko" (see Etymology below) is a species of gymnosperm tree native to East Asia.

This British businessman and adventurer, chairman of a Dubai-based aircraft brokerage, visited the South Pole multiple times and descended to the Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep before dying in 2023 when a submersible imploded in the North Atlantic - name him?
Hamish Harding (24 June 1964 - 18 June 2023) was a British businessman, pilot and adventurer based in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
Domesticated in Central Asia around 4000 BCE, this one-toed hoofed mammal evolved over 45 million years from the small, multi-toed Eohippus — what is it?
Horse (Equus ferus caballus) is a domesticated, one-toed, hoofed mammal.
Found in two forms — a grassland dweller and a darker scrubland cousin — this East and Southern African antelope's scientific name means 'black-footed high-horn.' Which animal?
Impala (Aepyceros melampus, lit. 'black-footed high-horn' in Ancient Greek) is a medium-sized antelope found in eastern and southern Africa.
Born in Albuquerque and a Princeton engineering graduate, this businessman founded and once ran Amazon, the e-commerce and cloud-computing giant — who is he?

Jeff Bezos (n Jorgensen; born January 12, 1964) is an American businessman, and the founder, executive chairman, and former president and CEO of Amazon, the world's largest e-commerce and cloud computing company.
Found from Africa to the Americas, this family of 118 bird species has big heads and sharp bills, and though most picture them by rivers, many actually live deep in forests — what are they?
Kingfisher are a family, the Alcedinidae, of small to medium-sized, brightly coloured birds in the order Coraciiformes.
This American computer scientist rose to prominence after Elon Musk praised his MIT study on Tesla's semi-autonomous driving system, and now hosts a long-form interview podcast. Who is he?
Lex Fridman (born 15 August 1983) is an American computer scientist and podcaster.

This medical condition involves lymph nodes that become abnormal in size or consistency, with its inflammatory form sometimes distinguished as lymphadenitis and its infectious neck form historically called scrofula — what is it called?
Lymphadenopathy is a disease of the lymph nodes, in which they are abnormal in size or consistency.
Among the first women in Canada to earn a medical doctorate, this physician-chemist is best remembered for a landmark 1913 enzyme-kinetics paper co-authored with Leonor Michaelis — who was she?
Maud Menten (March 20, 1879 - July 17, 1960) was a Canadian physician and chemist.
This dark-coated member of the weasel family comes in American and European species, plus an extinct 'sea' relative — what animal is it?

Mink are dark-coloured, semiaquatic, carnivorous mammals in the genera Mustela and Neogale and part of the family Mustelidae, which also includes weasels, stoats, martens, otters, badgers, and others.
This protective plate at fingertips and toe-tips is found in nearly every primate except marmosets, and is made of the same tough protein found in claws, hooves, and horns — what is it?

Nail (anatomy) is a protective plate characteristically found at the tip of the digits (fingers and toes) of almost all primates (except for marmosets), corresponding to the claws in other tetrapod animals.
This basic mathematical object is used to count, measure, and label, most commonly represented today through the Hindu-Arabic system of ten symbols — what fundamental concept is it?
Number is a mathematical object used to count, measure, and label. The most basic examples are the natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so forth.
Jointly built by Italy, the UK and Germany, this variable-sweep-wing combat aircraft comes in strike, electronic-warfare and interceptor variants — which jet?
Panavia Tornado is a family of twin-engine, variable-sweep wing multi-role combat aircraft, jointly developed and manufactured by Italy, the United Kingdom and Germany.
Dubbed the "father of transplantation," this Brazilian-born biologist shared a 1960 Nobel Prize for his discovery of acquired immune tolerance. Who was he?

Peter Medawar (28 February 1915 - 2 October 1987) was a Brazilian-born biologist and writer of Lebanese-British descent who, from a succession of research and teaching posts (Oxford through the Royal Institution), and senior U.K.
Which silvery-white precious metal carries the symbol Pt, leads group 10 of the periodic table, and is far rarer in Earth's crust than its glittering cousins?
Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.
Unfolding inside every cell in two acts called transcription and translation, this process turns a gene's DNA into messenger RNA on its way to building enzymes and hormones — what is it?
Protein biosynthesis is a core biological process, occurring inside cells, balancing the loss of cellular proteins (via degradation or export) through the production of fresh proteins.
Belonging to the genus Ribes and native to western Europe, which berry carries the scientific name Ribes rubrum and has spread into the wild in many regions?
Redcurrant (Ribes rubrum) is a member of the genus Ribes in the family Grossulariaceae.
Sitting in group 4 just below hafnium, this synthetic element named for a famous physicist has a most-stable isotope that survives only about 48 minutes — which element is it?
Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rf and atomic number 104.
Born into a Russian-Jewish family in Moscow and brought to the US at age six, which co-founder of Google served as president of Alphabet until 2019?
Sergey Brin (born August 21, 1973) is an American computer scientist and businessman who co-founded Google with Larry Page.
Which genus of about 28 grass species includes one member grown worldwide both as a cereal grain for human consumption and as fodder for livestock?
Sorghum (genus) is a genus of about 28 species of flowering plants in the grass family (Poaceae).
A single-seat, twin-engine, supermaneuverable 4.5-generation fighter derived from the Su-27, it was relabeled from "Su-27M" after the Soviet collapse to court export buyers — which Russian jet?
Sukhoi Su-35 (NATO reporting name: Flanker-E/M, occasionally nicknamed "Super Flanker") is the designation for two improved derivatives of the Su-27 air superiority fighter.
Used to treat asthma and COPD, this methylxanthine drug — a cousin of caffeine — turns up in trace amounts in tea, chocolate, and yerba mate. What is it?
Theophylline is a drug that inhibits phosphodiesterase and blocks adenosine receptors.
One of the earliest arthropod groups ever to appear in the fossil record, this extinct marine creature persisted in the oceans for nearly 270 million years across over 22,000 species — what is it?
Trilobite (meaning "three-lobed entities") are extinct marine arthropods that form the class Trilobita.

This English fashion designer, largely responsible for bringing punk fashion into the mainstream, ran a boutique on King's Road with her partner, whose band helped define the 1970s UK punk scene — who is she?

Vivienne Westwood (ne Swire; 8 April 1941 - 29 December 2022) was an English fashion designer and businesswoman, largely responsible for bringing modern punk and new wave fashions into the mainstream.

This Indian Islamic preacher and comparative-religion scholar delivers his speeches in English while wearing a suit and tie, and founded both a research foundation and a television channel called Peace TV — who is he?
Zakir Naik (born 18 October 1965) is an Indian Islamic da'i and orator who focuses on comparative religion.
Widespread across Europe and into East Asia, this venomous snake looms large in British folklore but rarely delivers a fatal bite — what reptile?
Adder: Species of venomous snake. Vipera berus, commonly known as the common European adder and the common European viper, is a species of venomous snake in the family Viperidae.
This Italian physicist built the first true electric battery in 1799 and discovered methane, disproving the idea that electricity could only come from living bodies — who is he?
Alessandro Volta: Italian chemist and physicist (1745–1827)
This highly soluble, hygroscopic crystalline salt is prized as a high-nitrogen fertilizer but is also the major ingredient in the industrial explosive ANFO — what is it?
Ammonium nitrate: Chemical compound with formula NH4NO3.
Useless against the cold, the flu, or any fungus, this kind of medicine works only by killing or stalling bacteria — what is it called?
Antibiotic: Antimicrobial substance active against bacteria.
Dubbed the 'Prophet of the Space Age,' this English science fiction author co-wrote the screenplay for 2001: A Space Odyssey and formed sci-fi's 'Big Three' with Heinlein and Asimov — who is he?
Arthur C. Clarke: British science fiction writer (1917–2008)

Flown by the Royal Air Force's Red Arrows display team, this British jet-powered advanced trainer has been license-built in India by Hindustan Aeronautics, with over 1,000 sold to 18 countries — which aircraft?
BAE Systems Hawk: Military training aircraft family.
Strawberries, blueberries, blackberries, and currants all fall under this small, pulpy, often brightly colored category of fruit — which Britain calls "soft fruit." What is it?
Berry: In the culinary sense, small edible fruit.
Announced in 2011, this fourth-generation narrow-body jet introduced more efficient LEAP engines and split-tip winglets, with variants from the 7 up through the 10 — what aircraft is it?
This volatile red-brown liquid element, with properties between chlorine and iodine, gets its name from the Greek word for 'stench' — which element?
Bromine: Chemical element with atomic number 35 (Br)
Designated Maryland's official state crustacean, this species is expected to benefit from climate change even as overfishing hurts other Chesapeake Bay fisheries — which species?
Callinectes sapidus: Species of crustacean. It is Maryland's largest commercial fishery and has been designated its state crustacean.
A wartime myth claimed eating this vegetable helped British pilots see in the dark — really a cover story for radar — which root vegetable?
Carrot: Root vegetable. The carrot (Daucus carota subsp. sativus) is a root vegetable in the umbellifer family Apiaceae.
In a joint presentation with Alfred Russel Wallace, this English naturalist unveiled the idea that the struggle for existence drives a process he likened to selective breeding — who was he?
Charles Darwin: English naturalist and biologist (1809–1882)
This genus native to South and Southeast Asia gave rise to oranges, lemons, and limes through extensive hybridization — what is it?

This medium-sized bird of prey ranges across Europe into northwestern China, hunting rodents like voles from a perch, with northern populations migrating as far as South Africa for winter — what bird is this?
Common buzzard: Species of bird of prey. It is a member of the genus Buteo in the family Accipitridae.

This blood-feeding parasitic insect, scientifically Pthirus pubis, typically lives in coarse body hair and diverged from a gorilla-infecting relative about 3.3 million years ago — what is it commonly called?
Crab louse: Species of insect. The crab louse or pubic louse (Pthirus pubis) is an insect that is an obligate ectoparasite of humans, feeding exclusively on blood.
This Swedish tech entrepreneur founded and chairs a streaming giant, with a net worth estimated at $8.7 billion in December 2025 — who is he?
This bodily process breaks large food molecules into water-soluble components through both mechanical action like chewing and chemical action from enzymes — what's it called?
Digestion: Biological process of breaking down food.
Sometimes nicknamed 'math dyslexia' even though it's a distinct condition, this learning disorder involves persistent difficulty understanding numbers and performing calculations — what is it called?
This Italian-American physicist discovered two elements, technetium and astatine, plus the antiproton — the last earning him a share of the 1959 Nobel Prize in Physics. Who was he?
Emilio Segrè: Italian-American nuclear physicist and radiochemist (1905–1989)
Marketed under brand names like Arcoxia, this selective COX-2 inhibitor developed by Merck was approved in 63 countries by 2007 — everywhere, notably, except the United States — what is the drug?
This membranous bodily structure comes in superficial, visceral, and deep types, and a dangerous pressure buildup within it can cause compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Fascia: Layer of connective tissue in the body.

Members of this insect order have just one pair of true wings — the hindwings evolved into balance organs called halteres — and the group includes mosquitoes among its 150,000+ species. What are they commonly called?
Fly: Order of insects. A fly (pl. flies) is an insect of the order Diptera (from Ancient Greek δι- di- 'two' and πτερόν pteron 'wing'), named for the single pair of wings.
Caused by a loss of blood supply and marked by skin turning red or black, this condition comes in dry, wet, and gas forms — what is it?
Gangrene: Type of tissue death by ischemia.

Inducted into the U.S. Air Force Hall of Fame in 2018, this American mathematician modeled the precise shape of the Earth — work later baked into the Global Positioning System that now guides your phone. Who is she?
Designed specifically for airborne early warning rather than adapted from an existing airframe, this twin-turboprop carrier plane replaced the piston-engined Tracer for the US Navy — which aircraft?
Grumman E-2 Hawkeye: Airborne early warning and control aircraft. The Northrop Grumman E-2 Hawkeye is an American all-weather, carrier-capable, tactical airborne early warning (AEW) aircraft.
Nicknamed bindwood or lovestone, this clinging evergreen native to Europe scales tree trunks, walls, and fences — which plant?
Hedera helix: Species of flowering plant.

Widely credited as the 'father of the Indian nuclear programme,' this theoretical physicist founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and chaired India's first Atomic Energy Commission — who is it?
Homi J. Bhabha: Indian nuclear physicist (1909–1966)
It usually causes no symptoms at all, yet this persistently elevated arterial pressure is a leading cause of stroke, heart failure and premature death worldwide — what's the medical name for it?
Hypertension: Long-term high blood pressure in the arteries.
This concept in calculus, a continuous analog of a sum, computes the signed area under a curve and pairs with differentiation as one of the field's two fundamental operations?
This fragrant genus of shrubs and vines in the olive family is grown in vast quantities in one Egyptian village that supplies much of the world's perfume industry — which plant?
Jasmine: Genus of flowering plant in the olive family Oleaceae.
Born Giulia Maddalena Angela in Italy, this physician became a leading freethinker and activist for women's rights and social reform in early-20th-century Argentina — who is she?
Julieta Lanteri: Argentine doctor and activist (1873–1932)
Nocturnal, owl-faced, and unable to fly, this endangered New Zealand bird holds the title of the world's heaviest parrot. What is it?
Kākāpō: Parrot endemic to New Zealand. It is the only parrot to have a polygynous lek breeding system.
This synthetic thyroid hormone treats hypothyroidism, has a half-life of roughly 7.5 days, and is not intended for weight loss — what's this medication?
Levothyroxine: Thyroid hormone medication. Levothyroxine, also known as L-thyroxine, is a synthetic form of the thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4).
Patented in 1980 and marketed as Claritin, this second-generation antihistamine treats hay fever and hives but can still cause sleepiness and dry mouth — what is it?
Loratadine: Antihistamine medication. Loratadine, sold under the brand name Claritin among others, is a medication used to treat allergies.
Genetically related to the Bichon, Bolognese, and Havanese, this toy breed sports a silky white coat, doesn't shed, and tops out around 4 kilograms — what breed is it?
Maltese dog: Breed of toy dog. The precise link, if any, between the modern and ancient breeds is not known.

Entering US Navy service in 1961 before the Marines and Air Force adopted it too, this twin-engine supersonic jet became America's most-produced supersonic military aircraft with 5,195 built — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II: Fighter aircraft family developed from 1958.
Sold as Flagyl, this antibiotic and antiprotozoal fights everything from giardiasis to trichomoniasis — but it's notorious for leaving a metallic taste in your mouth — what is it?
Metronidazole: Antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication. Metronidazole, sold under the brand name Flagyl and Metrogyl among others, is an antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication.
Making up about 23% of all named marine organisms, this phylum is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after the arthropods — what is it?
This condition describes an abnormally dilated pupil that remains enlarged even in bright light, often triggered by trauma, disease, or certain drugs — what is it called?
Mydriasis: Excessive dilation of the pupil.
Providing the basis for Newtonian mechanics, these physical laws relate an object's motion to the forces acting on it. How many are there?
Newton's laws of motion are three physical laws that describe the relationship between the motion of an object and the forces acting on it, providing the basis for Newtonian mechanics.
First described by Linnaeus in 1758, this medium-sized spotted wild cat hunts armadillos and opossums at twilight across a range from the southwestern US to South America — what cat is it?
Ocelot: Species of wild cat. It is native to the southwestern United States, Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean islands of Trinidad and Margarita.

Most members of this order of over 200 species are solitary night hunters with broad heads, binocular vision, and feathers tuned for silent flight — though oddballs like the burrowing kind break the mold. What are they?
Owl: Birds from the order Strigiformes.
This Stanford biologist became famous — and controversial — for his 1968 book warning that runaway population growth would bring famine and resource depletion. Who was he?
This inherited metabolic disorder, caused by mutations in the PAH gene, leaves patients unable to break down a certain amino acid and can give off a musty odor if untreated — what is it?
Phenylketonuria: Amino acid metabolic disorder. Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inborn error of metabolism that results in decreased metabolism of the amino acid phenylalanine.
First classified as its own fossil order in 1835, this group of Mesozoic marine reptiles thrived through the Jurassic before dying out at the end of the Cretaceous — what are they called?
Plesiosaur: Order of reptiles (fossil). The Plesiosauria or plesiosaurs are an order or clade of extinct Mesozoic marine reptiles, belonging to the Sauropterygia.
This New World family within the order Carnivora encompasses raccoons, ringtails, coatis, and kinkajous, most of them omnivorous — what family is it?
Procyonidae: Family of mammals. Procyonidae ( PROH-see-ON-i-dee) is a New World family of the order Carnivora.
Native to southern China, this pear tree's fruit goes by dozens of names worldwide - Asian pear, apple pear, nashi pear - but is rarely baked into pies due to its high water content - which species?
Pyrus pyrifolia: Species of pear with round crisp grainy fruit.
Rooted in Minangkabau cooking at the crossroads of the Malacca Strait, this dish slow-cooks meat in spiced coconut milk until the oil separates and it fries in its own glaze — what is it?

Nicknamed the 'dark lady of DNA,' this X-ray crystallographer's crucial contributions to the discovery of DNA's structure went largely unrecognized in her lifetime — James Watson believed she'd have won a Nobel Prize had she lived. Who was she?
Also called Besnier–Boeck–Schaumann disease, this non-infectious condition forms clusters of inflammatory cells called granulomata, often starting in the lungs, skin, or lymph nodes — what is it?
Sarcoidosis: Abnormal formation of clumps of inflammatory cells (granulomata)
About 90% of this mood-regulating neurotransmitter is actually made in your gut, where it controls intestinal movement, rather than the brain — also known as 5-HT, what is it?
Serotonin: Monoamine neurotransmitter. It is involved in mood, cognition, reward, learning, memory, and physiological processes such as vomiting and vasoconstriction.
With the formula CH3COONa, this colorless, moisture-absorbing compound is the salt formed from acetic acid — what is it called?
Named in 1880 from Greek words meaning 'bunch of grapes,' this genus of spherical, grape-clustered bacteria can grow with or without oxygen — which genus?
Comprising around 90 species split between river martins and all other members, this family of aerial-feeding songbirds is thought to have evolved as hole-nesters in Africa — what are they called?
Swallow: Family of songbirds. The term "swallow" is used as the common name for Hirundo rustica in the United Kingdom and Ireland.

Found at the ends of linear chromosomes, this repetitive DNA region works with specialized proteins to prevent the chromosome tip from being mistaken for a damaging double-strand break — what is it called?
Telomere: Region of repetitive nucleotide sequences on chromosomes.
The largest cat of the genus Panthera, this Asian apex predator wears orange fur with mostly vertical black stripes and ranges from snowy Russian forests to tropical Indian jungles — what is it?
Closely related to salmon, these carnivorous freshwater fish spawn in shallow gravel beds of headwater creeks after migrating upstream — what are they called?
Trout: Freshwater fish from subfamily Salmoninae.
Used to treat epilepsy and stabilize mood in bipolar disorder, this medication carries a serious risk of birth defects if taken during pregnancy — what is it?
Valproate: Medication used for epilepsy, bipolar disorder and migraine. Common side effects of valproate include nausea, vomiting, somnolence, and dry mouth.
Also known as ash pumpkin or winter melon, this South and Southeast Asian plant is grown for its very large fruit, eaten as a vegetable once mature — which plant?
Wax gourd: Species of vine and edible fruit.
This Japanese media artist and academic directs a research centre for 'Digital Nature' and holds visiting professorships at multiple Japanese art universities — who is he?
Yoichi Ochiai: Japanese academic, artist, and entrepreneur. Yoichi Ochiai (落合 陽一, Yoichi Ochiai; born 16 September 1987) is a Japanese media artist, entrepreneur, and academic.
What is the chemical symbol for tin?
The symbol for tin is Sn. Tin is a chemical element; it has the symbol Sn and atomic number 50.
What is the chemical symbol for copernicium?
The symbol for copernicium is Cn. Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.

In what year was Jamie Lee Curtis born?
Jamie Lee Curtis (born November 22, 1958) is an American actress, producer, and children's author.
In what year was Michelle Pfeiffer born?
Michelle Pfeiffer: Michelle Marie Pfeiffer ( FY-fər; born April 29, 1958) is an American actress and producer.
In what year was Vin Diesel born?
Vin Diesel: Mark Sinclair Vincent (born July 18, 1967), known professionally as Vin Diesel, is an American actor and filmmaker.
In what year was Benicio del Toro born?
Benicio del Toro: Benicio Monserrate Rafael del Toro Sánchez (Latin American Spanish: [beˈnisjo ðel ˈtoɾo]; born February 19, 1967) is a Puerto Rican actor.
In what year was Rose Byrne born?
Rose Byrne: Mary Rose Byrne (born 24 July 1979) is an Australian actress.
In what year was Andrew Garfield born?
Andrew Garfield: Andrew Russell Garfield (born 20 August 1983) is an English and American actor.
In what year was Liev Schreiber born?
Liev Schreiber: Isaac Liev Schreiber ( LEE-ev SHRY-bər; born October 4, 1967) is an American actor.
In what year was Anne Hathaway born?
Anne Hathaway: Anne Jacqueline Hathaway (born November 12, 1982) is an American actress.
In what year was Dave Bautista born?
Dave Bautista: David Michael Bautista Jr. (born January 18, 1969) is an American actor and retired professional wrestler.
In what year was Chris Hemsworth born?
Chris Hemsworth: Christopher Hemsworth (born 11 August 1983) is an Australian actor and film producer.
